problem: Existing VLN agents encode the whole trajectory as a single sequence (LSTM/transformer), so erroneous steps and backtracking (error-and-correction) get mixed with ordinary steps and the fine-grained structure is lost. Performance drops sharply when errors are manually injected at the start.
motivation: About 10% of R2R val-unseen episodes of RecBert/VLN-HAMT involve at least one error-and-correction even on 4-6 step paths. Sequential encoders must compare adjacent steps to detect reversals. Injecting k-step error-and-correction at the start causes large SR drops for baselines but not for the proposed agent. Erroneous steps are still useful context, so they should be kept but separated.
key_idea: Organize the trajectory as a tree rooted at the start, where error-and-corrections become deprecated branches, and encode it with a Tree-Transformer, a tree-based long-range backtracking action space, and a Tree-nDTW reward on the current root-to-node path.
insight: Making the branching structure explicit lets the agent separate failed attempts from the current attempt, so it backtracks more (#BT 0.99 vs 0.52-0.65 for other rewards) and corrects errors better. Ablations show each part adds SR: tree 0.59→0.61, +action 0.63, +reward 0.62, all three 0.68. Removing depth embedding and tree attention (vanilla transformer) drops SR to 0.63. The filter size k peaks in the middle (k=5), since older backtrack candidates add noise.
method: Trajectory tree: The root is the start. A move to a new neighbor creates a child node. A move to a visited neighbor only updates the pointer. Backtracking creates no node, so failed attempts remain as deprecated branches.

Tree-Transformer: Replaces the position embedding with a learnable per-depth embedding. Replaces dense self-attention with a mask so each node attends only to its ancestors and descendants, keeping global information flow through the root.

Tree-based action space: Replaces the backtrack action with forward moves from all post-backtracking nodes (e.g. 'hb' means backtrack to b, then step to h). The agent is transferred along the recorded path, and executed actions are excluded. Candidate views are attached as virtual leaf nodes.
Dynamic filtering: A FIFO queue keeps only the k=5 most recently visited nodes as post-backtracking candidates. About 80% of backtracks target nodes visited in the last 5 steps.
Tree-nDTW reward: nDTW is computed on the current pursuing path (root to current node). Non-stop steps get the nDTW increment. The stop step gets success indicator + nDTW.

Holistic agent: An LXMERT-style cross-modal transformer, with Tree-Transformer replacing the visual self-attention. The instruction CLS token is fused with each candidate view, and a 2-layer FC network scores each action.

setting.backbone: LXMERT-style cross-modal transformer with Tree-Transformer (trained; details in supplementary)
setting.training_data: R2R and RxR training data (pretraining/augmentation details not given in the main text; RxR multilingual model)
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB views at discrete graph viewpoints
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints, extended with tree-based long-range backtrack+forward actions (filtered to the recent k=5 nodes)

numbers.extra: tree-based action space, Tree-nDTW reward, k=5
numbers.evidence: Table 1, R2R val-unseen: Ours 0.68 3.49 17.31 0.57 (SR/SPL printed as fractions)

numbers_note: R2R metrics are printed as fractions in the paper; SR and SPL are converted to percent here, and NE and TL are as printed. RxR is reported in percent.
results: On R2R the agent reaches SR 68% on val-unseen and 66% on test, beating VLN-HAMT (66/65) and RecBert (63/63), but with a longer TL (17.31/19.62) and SPL equal to or below the baselines (val-unseen SPL 0.57 vs 0.61 for HAMT). On RxR it also has the best SR (58.7 val-unseen, 54.1 test vs HAMT 56.5/53.1), with lower SPL and nDTW.
limitations: Long trajectories (TL 17-20 m) lower SPL and nDTW compared with VLN-HAMT, because of long-range transfers and a reward that does not penalize them.
Val-seen SR is lower than VLN-HAMT (0.75 vs 0.76), and the action space grows with the tree, requiring a heuristic filter (k=5).
Evaluated only in discrete-graph settings (R2R and RxR), with no continuous-environment or real-robot tests.
